_about: The renderer prototype's defaults, copied from the design doc (Prototype > Parameters and defaults) and the prototype's constants. UNTUNED PLACEHOLDERS: tuning is carried over to the first variant board (design doc, Decision workflow > Carried over). Code reads these; none of them is a decision until a variant board makes it one and data/decisions/decisions.json records it.

source.design_doc: Prototype > Parameters and defaults; Style rules > Palette

brush_size.affects: Brush radius; enclosure size = 2.6 x brush

collision_check.affects: Rejects overlaps; clears sites under structures

tree_height.affects: Height as a multiple of radius

sun_direction.affects: Shadow direction, roof and slope shading; 315 = NW

line_weight.affects: All ink; per-element multipliers are under linework

aircraft_shadow_altitude_scale.affects: A plane's shadow is cast as if it flew at altitude x this (600 m up casts like 6 m), so the gap grows with height and closes near the ground

render_passes._about: Draw order, bottom to top, and the prototype's default toggles.

accents._about: Side colours (Alex 2026-10-09, decision unit-sheet-choices). Equal OKLCH lightness and chroma: side_a oklch(0.551 0.100 30), side_b oklch(0.551 0.100 260). One accent zone per unit: wing roundels, the tank's engine-deck panel, the battery's ground panel, the cruiser's quarterdeck, the radio hut roof. Alex: worth mirroring in the HUD.

linework._about: Style rules > Linework: multipliers on line_weight per element.

pen._about: How an ink line's width varies along it (Alex 2026-10-09, decision pen-line, option C 'shadow side'): a closed outline is thin on edges facing the sun and heavy on edges facing away; open lines are a fixed fraction with tapered ends. Width = line weight x element multiplier x these factors. prototype_default is the prototype's even line, used by --parity.

detail_light._about: Fixed top-left light for interior detail (florets, stipple), independent of the sun. A prototype choice, not read from the reference.

map_view._about: The map view (Track V, scripts/render/map_view.gd and chunk_*.gd): the static map baked into chunk textures under a camera. EVERY VALUE IS PROPOSED by Track V (2026-10-09); none is a decision. Scale is NOT here: px_per_m is Track T's (data/terrain/terrain.json scale.px_per_m).

provider._reason: terrain = Track T's levels, hachures and groves (scripts/world/terrain.gd); scene = the prototype's scene generator per chunk (forts, houses, props, trees, no terrain), the stand-in

chunk_px._reason: one power-of-two texture per chunk (4 MB RGBA8, 5.3 MB with mipmaps); the baker's tiling, independent of the provider's own generation cells

prefetch_chunks._reason: chunks baked beyond the view on every side, so a pan at a fighter's turn speed (~380 px/s at 4 px/m) meets baked ground

keep_chunks._reason: chunks further than this from the view are dropped first when the cache is full

max_cached_chunks._reason: about 340 MB of chunk textures; a 1280x720 view at zoom 0.5 shows 12 chunks

max_jobs._reason: chunks in the bake pipeline at once. Was 8 (Track V: most of a job's time is waiting, so more jobs keep the worker threads busy). CHANGED to 4 (map-performance track, 2026-10-10, PROPOSED), measured cold on the sandbox's first view (12 chunks, three runs each, strict nearest-first stepping and the ring held back): 2 jobs first chunk 2.7 s / view 12.9 s / ring 29.0 s; 3 jobs 3.2 / 10.8 / 24.3; 4 jobs 2.9 / 9.9 / 22.6; 8 jobs 4.5 / 9.4 / 21.1. With nearest-first stepping the first chunk lands about 1.6 s sooner with 4 than with 8 and the view is complete about 0.5 s later; each job holds its 4096 px supersampled render targets for the frame or two it renders

max_worker_tasks._reason: worker threads the baker uses at once: GDScript scales to about 8 threads and then slows down (measured on 32: 256 tree sprites in 820 ms serial, 131 ms on 8, 475 ms on 16, 840 ms on 31)

collect_delay_frames._reason: extra frames between drawing a baked canvas and asking for its pixels. The read-back is asynchronous, so 0; a synchronous read-back (a renderer without a RenderingDevice) waits for every frame in flight -- a sprite page cost ~190 ms of main thread the next frame, ~25 ms four frames later

bake_budget_ms._reason: main-thread time the baker may take per frame (recording runs on worker threads and is not counted)

ring_after_view._reason: PROPOSED by the map-performance track (2026-10-10): the prefetch ring is only REQUESTED once every chunk of the view is baked (and the view's chunks under the fog before the ring). A ring job started while a view chunk was missing took a job slot, worker threads and the main thread's budget from the chunk the player was waiting for. false: the old behaviour, view and ring requested together (priorities still put the view first)

priority_offsets._reason: PROPOSED (map-performance track): added to a chunk's distance from the view centre (in chunks) to rank bake requests, lower first: a view chunk wholly under the fog's opaque topographic layer (nobody sees it until a unit's sight reaches it) after the visible ones; the prefetch ring after the view; a fogged ring chunk after the other ring chunks. Larger than any distance, so each group finishes first. Needs map_view.hidden_test (the sandbox sets it to the fog layer's rect_under_fog)

prefetch_ahead_extra_chunks._reason: PROPOSED (map-performance track): while the camera is moving (prefetch_motion_min_chunks_per_s) the ring reaches this many chunks further ahead of it than prefetch_chunks

prefetch_behind_chunks._reason: PROPOSED (map-performance track): while the camera is moving, the ring behind it (the side it left) is this deep; 0 asks for nothing there (chunks already baked stay until the cache cap drops the furthest). prefetch_chunks applies when the camera is still, and to the sides across its motion

prefetch_motion_window_s._reason: PROPOSED (map-performance track): the camera's recent motion is its view centre's displacement over this many seconds (a jump of the camera counts as motion for this long)

prefetch_motion_min_chunks_per_s._reason: PROPOSED (map-performance track): slower than this (chunks of the view centre per second over the window) the camera counts as still and the ring is the same on every side

prefetch_bias._reason: PROPOSED (map-performance track): ring chunks ahead of the camera's motion rank this many chunks nearer than they are, those behind it as many further (priority = distance - bias x cosine of the angle to the motion)

sprite_pages_per_frame._reason: PROPOSED (map-performance track, 2026-10-10): sprite pages whose sprites may be submitted to the GPU in one frame, nearest chunk's first; 0 no cap. A page of 24 sprites is about 12 ms of GPU if it all lands in one frame; several submitting together pile up in the same frames. Measured cold on the sandbox's first view with 4 jobs, three runs each, cap 0 / 1 / 2 / 4: first chunk 3.0 / 5.8 / 3.7 / 3.1 s, view complete 10.2 / 15.1 / 10.2 / 9.8 s, frames over 33 ms 8 / 1 / 5.7 / 15 (one noisy run), worst frame 46 / 35 / 37 / 44 ms. 1 starves the bake; 2 keeps the bake's pace and takes the worst frames down

bake_budget_loading_ms._reason: PROPOSED (map-performance track, 2026-10-10): main-thread milliseconds a frame the baker may take while map_view.bake_boost is on (the sandbox sets it while its loading card is up, when a long frame costs nothing) instead of bake_budget_ms. Measured cold on the sandbox's first view, three runs each, budget 6 / 10 / 14 ms: view complete 11.3 / 10.1 / 10.0 s, first chunk 3.9 / 3.6 / 3.5 s, but frames over 33 ms 8 / 16 / 94 and worst frame 42 / 45 / 73 ms - so 6 ms while playing, 14 only behind the card (the main thread is not what limits a bake: the terrain generator's serial lane is)

sprite_batch._reason: sprites recorded per worker task; each sprite is its own small canvas (a canvas group costs a render pass over its whole target, so shared atlas pages were ~70x dearer on the GPU)

sprite_cache_max._reason: sprites kept across chunks, least recently used dropped first: about 50 chunks' worth of trees

zoom._reason: placeholders until Track F sets the zoom limits; 0.25 shows about 5 x 3 chunks

pan._reason: WASD / arrows, the screen edges, or a middle- or right-button drag

tree_pool._reason: OFF: CHANGES THE LOOK. One sprite per (radius bucket, variant) shared by every tree in it, instead of one sprite per tree: about 55 buckets x 16 variants, so tree sprite cost stops growing with the map. No rotation or mirroring (a sprite's lit side and shadow-side pen are baked in world orientation). Off until Alex has seen the side-by-side.

standin._reason: the scene provider only: per chunk, the chance of the prototype's fort, of a house and of a prop cluster; structures stay this far inside their chunk so none crosses a border
